rows.text:
Complete the following by choosing the correct answers from the bracket:
(a) In uniform circular motion the **centrifugal force** acts __________ *[towards the centre / away from the centre / along the tangential direction]*.
(b) Refractive index of a medium is **independent** of __________ *[temperature / angle of incidence / wavelength of light]*.
(c) Heat absorbed during **change of phase** depends on __________ *[mass / change in temperature / specific heat capacity]* of the substance.
(d) Emf of a cell is __________ *[greater than / less than / equal to]* the terminal voltage when the cell is in **open circuit**.
(e) In a step-up transformer the **turns ratio** is __________ *[more than 1 / less than 1 / equal to 1]*.
(f) The nuclear radiation with **lowest** ionizing power is __________ *[\(\alpha\) / \(\beta\) / \(\gamma\)]*.
rows._flag: Six independent 1-mark fill-ins spanning six chapters (Force, Refraction at Plane Surfaces, Calorimetry, Current Electricity, Electromagnetism, Radioactivity); filed under the first. Main session may prefer to split it.

rows.text:

(c) the kinetic energy of Richa at point **R**. *(While moving from **Q** to **R**, she loses 500 J of energy against friction.)*

figure.note: Richa on a skateboard at the top point P of a curved track that falls to Q on the ground and rises to R; R is marked 3m above the ground. Label: Ground.

figure.note: Two sonometer boxes A and B, each with a wire over two bridges a length l apart, a paper rider on the wire, and the wire passing over a pulley to a hanging 10 kgf weight. The wire on A is drawn visibly THICKER than the wire on B.

rows.subtopic: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity
rows.text:
(a) A certain amount of heat will warm 1 g of material **X** by \(10^\circ\)C and 1 g of material **Y** by \(40^\circ\)C. Which material has **higher** specific heat capacity?
(b) Which material, **X** or **Y**, would you select to make a calorimeter?
(c) The specific heat capacity of a substance remains the **same** when it changes its state from solid to liquid. State **True** or **False.**

A copper rod **PQ** carrying current is kept in a magnetic field as shown in the diagram.
(a) The copper rod **PQ** will move towards **C**. State **True** or **False**.
(b) **Name** the law used to determine the direction of motion of **PQ**.
(c) What will be the effect on the force experienced, if the rod **PQ** is replaced by another copper rod of **same** length but of **greater** cross-sectional area?
(d) Justify your answer in (c).

figure.note: Two vertical bar magnets, one above and one below, each labelled S (top) and N (bottom), so the upper magnet's N faces the lower magnet's S. Between them a copper rod PQ (P lower-left, Q upper-right) lies across two horizontal rails connected to a cell. Labels C (left of the rod) and A (right of the rod) mark the two directions of motion.
